facts.text: La Granja means "the farm" in Spanish, reflecting its origins as expansive agricultural land owned by Bernardo O'Higgins after Chile’s independence.
The commune was officially created on November 18, 1892, by Law No. 1, separating it from the Department of La Victoria in Santiago Province.
During the 1980s, residents of La Granja’s La Bandera neighborhood staged a land takeover to demand affordable housing amid a regime that favored market solutions.
The local Metro La Granja station, part of Santiago’s Line 1, was damaged by arson during the 2019 social protests that saw residents mobilize against high living costs.
La Granja’s transformation from elite-owned estates to a suburban commune mirrors Santiago’s broader urban expansion driven by industrialization and rural migration in the mid‑20th century.
The commune’s name derives from an early landowner associated with a farmstead, a detail that ties its identity to the region’s agrarian past.
